iconicAnchor.label: Gold-ground Byzantine sacred mosaic
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Historic tesserae and sacred image programs establish how reflective material, architectural placement, frontal figures, and hierarchy work together beyond a generic gold pixel texture.

sources.title: Mosaic Tesserae
supports: Glass and gold tesserae create a directional, irregular reflective field whose behavior depends on material and architectural light.

sources.title: Icons and Iconoclasm in Byzantium
supports: Byzantine sacred images carry theological, historical, and devotional functions that cannot be reduced to a decorative facial formula.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches tessellated, gold leaf, iconic, flat, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/byzantine-mosaic/reference-02.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.

culturalContext.note: Treat Byzantine sacred mosaics as historically situated Christian devotional works, not a generic luxury texture. Identify site, date, subject, and present custodial context; use non-sacred movement-level approximations for commercial outputs unless the task specifically requires and supports sacred content.
